task: per-minute apnea-like heartbeat-timing cue (research prototype, not a diagnosis)

input.signal: three-lead ECG (red, black, white electrodes), one ECG waveform analyzed
input.window: 60 s minute, with +-2 minute context (5 minute window)
input.preprocessing: XQRS beat detection (wfdb) in 10 minute chunks; R-R kept if 0.3 to 2.0 s

neighbor_order_note: neighbors are appended in order k = -1, +1, -2, +2; a low-quality neighbor contributes four zeros
classifier: features clipped to the training 1-99 percent range, then StandardScaler + logistic regression (C=0.5, class_weight balanced), threshold 0.5, exported to model.json (29 weights)
training_data: PhysioNet Apnea-ECG: 35 labeled records, 15,790 usable minutes, per-minute apnea reference labels (the only apnea-labeled source; none of the datasets named in the Track 2 manual has apnea labels; it comes from the PhysioNet physiological databases the manual references)

WESAD (named in the manual): 15 healthy volunteers, chest ECG, awake states (baseline, stress, amusement, meditation, transitions), 1,348 usable minutes, used as non-apnea awake examples. ASSUMPTION: none of them was screened for sleep apnea.
split: record or subject level 5-fold GroupKFold over Apnea-ECG records (c05 and c06 grouped) and WESAD subjects; clipping bounds and normalization fit inside training folds only

held_out_results.v3_for_comparison: AUROC 0.814, sensitivity 0.702, specificity 0.805, WESAD false alarm 0.251 (Apnea-ECG only)

safeguards: scores clip features to the training 1-99 percent range
abstains (UNKNOWN: outside trained range) when 6 or more of 29 features fall outside the training 0.5-99.5 percent range; about 2 percent of training minutes
limitations: trained on overnight sleep recordings; scores while awake, moving or talking are not meaningful
single public dataset, not tested on AFE4950 recordings yet
ECG only; PPG not in the model
dashboard scores lag by about 3 minutes (2 minute lookahead)
scores on bundled demo records are in-sample
gate_test_only: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database (named in the manual): 48 records, 1,440 minutes, used only to test the quality gate and out-of-range guard (12 percent of minutes abstained); no apnea labels, so no accuracy claim.

apnea_ecg_test_set_x01_x35.note: 35 PhysioNet test records never used in training

osasud_stroke_unit_30_patients.note: different population, monitor ECG at 80 Hz, positives include hypopnea; the ECG model did NOT transfer

ppg_breathing_pause_detector_osasud.tuned_sensitivity: about 0.5 at roughly 24 false alarms per hour
ppg_breathing_pause_detector_osasud.verdict: breathing/PPG did not add to the ECG score in this test and is not accurate enough to claim apnea detection
